LHX.sentence: L3Harris ticked up slightly, and while its profit margins are running a bit below their usual range, steady defense spending means the underlying story is unchanged.

ASML.sentence: ASML pulled back about 5% and is now sitting right around a level it often bounces from — nothing has changed about their monopoly on the machines that print the world's most advanced chips.

LIN.sentence: Linde is quietly ticking up, though there's a faint early sign that borrowing costs for its customers are creeping higher, which could soften demand a year or so out — worth watching but not yet a worry.

MSFT.sentence: Microsoft is calm — its Azure cloud business is still growing fast on the back of AI, and that story keeps grinding along without drama ahead of the next earnings update.

TMO.sentence: Thermo Fisher slipped slightly but is still near its highs after a strong month, as labs and drugmakers keep buying the equipment and supplies it sells to the whole life-sciences industry.

ENB.sentence: Enbridge is roughly flat, held back mainly by high interest rates making its steady pipeline dividend look less generous by comparison — the toll-road business itself is fine.

NOW.sentence: ServiceNow climbed again and is outpacing its software peers — big companies and government agencies keep buying its workflow-automation and AI tools, and investors are eagerly buying every dip.

GLNCY.sentence: Glencore held up well even as copper prices fell sharply, because its giant commodity-trading arm makes money from market swings and cushions the mining side.

MLM.sentence: Martin Marietta is barely moved, and the price it actually gets for a ton of crushed stone is still rising nicely — its quarries-you-can't-compete-with advantage remains fully intact.

KOF.sentence: The Latin American Coca-Cola bottler is basically flat, with a slightly weaker Mexican peso creating a small drag when its earnings get converted back to dollars.

PBR.A.sentence: Petrobras is steady, and with oil prices far above what it costs the company to pump a barrel, there's plenty of cash flowing to support its very large dividend.

AMKBY.sentence: Maersk, the Danish container-shipping giant, slipped a bit, but its stock is priced below what its fleet of ships would cost to replace — a built-in cushion if trade stays slow.

MA.sentence: Mastercard rose a bit and, unusually, is trading at about the same price as rival Visa rather than its typical premium, even as people keep tapping their cards more than ever.

ISRG.sentence: No fresh data on the da Vinci surgical robot maker today, so there's nothing new to report.
